title: Upgrade Prompt Editor with Embedded Code Regions
summary: Convert the prompt box from a plain TextBox to a RichTextBox so it can host collapsible embedded code regions, add triple-backtick fence creation/collapse, and add Up/Down boundary navigation across those regions — all without regressing ordinary plain-text typing, voice dictation, or existing transcript code-block styling.

tasks.title: Convert PromptTextBox to RichTextBox foundation
tasks.description:
Replace the existing TextBox-based prompt editor control with a RichTextBox-based implementation that preserves the current plain-text typing experience and voice dictation integration.

## Observable outcome

The prompt editor renders and behaves as a RichTextBox internally while ordinary plain-text usage (typing, placeholder/watermark display, auto-grow/resize, scrollbar behavior, selection highlight, caret and line rendering) is intended to remain visually and behaviorally equivalent to the prior TextBox. Because a TextBox→RichTextBox control-type migration can introduce subtle rendering differences that automated tests cannot truthfully rule out, final confirmation of plain-text appearance/interaction parity is a human observation recorded at the plan's approval gate rather than a claim made by this task alone.

## Consumers

Tasks 002 and 003 build embedded-region creation, collapse, and boundary navigation on top of this RichTextBox foundation; the existing voice dictation pipeline continues to target this control.

## Constraints

Do not change the public surface voice dictation uses to insert text. Preserve existing data-binding and focus behavior used elsewhere in the prompt workflow.

tasks.title: Add triple-backtick embedded region creation and collapse
tasks.description:
On the RichTextBox foundation from task 001, detect a triple-backtick fence typed or pasted into the prompt editor and convert its contents into a collapsible embedded code region, with a serialization contract that round-trips the region back into a triple-backtick fenced block when the prompt is read.

## Observable outcome

Typing or pasting a triple-backtick fence in the prompt editor creates a visually distinct, collapsible embedded region; collapsing and expanding it works interactively; reading the prompt back out serializes the region into an equivalent triple-backtick fenced block.

## Consumers

Task 003 adds Up/Down caret navigation across these regions. The prompt serialization path (wherever the prompt text is read for submission) consumes the fence output produced here.

## Scope boundary

Language tagging on a fence is a serialization-contract capability only in this plan: a region may carry an optional language value that is included in the serialized fence, but no interactive language-picker UI ships as part of this task. A full language-selection UI is out of scope and deferred to a future plan.

scrutinyHistory.summary: Step 2 — embedded code region creation and collapse — is fully and accurately delivered. EmbeddedFenceDetector provides pure fence-detection/serialization logic; EmbeddedCodeRegionManager performs real FlowDocument segment surgery and is genuinely wired into MainWindow.PromptTextBox_TextChanged behind a correct reentrancy guard (the guard prevents infinite recursion from the nested TextChanged events caused by Document.Blocks.Clear(), it does not disable detection — the outer call still runs the conversion loop before returning). EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock is a real interactive Border/ToggleButton control reusing CopyableCodeBlockBuilder's Consolas/CodeSurface/CodeText convention verbatim (confirmed by direct comparison), with SetCollapsed() producing an observable visual toggle (TextBox vs TextBlock visibility swap), not a no-op property. RichTextBoxExtensions.GetPlainText() correctly serializes BlockUIContainer-hosted EmbeddedCodeRegionBlocks via ToFencedText() and leaves plain paragraphs unaffected. EmbeddedCodeRegionTests.cs exercises the real production classes (verified via csproj linked-file diff, not a reimplementation) end-to-end and concretely covers both normative contract examples plus a no-regression case. No language-picker UI was added — Language is purely a settable string property, consistent with scope. Ran the targeted filter myself: 45/45 passed, exactly matching the claim. Ran the full suite twice: one run showed 4 failures matching the claimed count/names exactly (7744/7748); a second run showed one apparent flake in the same pre-existing DPI/pixel-rendering tests, confirming no new regression. One minor, non-blocking nit: EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock.Language (string) hides FrameworkElement.Language (CultureInfo) producing CS0108, which should ideally use 'new' or a renamed property, but it causes no functional defect and is unrelated to task-owned scope.

tasks.title: Add Up/Down boundary navigation across embedded regions
tasks.description:
Implement Up/Down arrow-key caret navigation so the caret moves correctly into, through, and out of a collapsed or expanded embedded region at its top and bottom boundaries, rather than getting stuck or jumping unpredictably.

## Observable outcome

Pressing Up at the first line below a region moves the caret into the region (or past it, per the region's current collapsed/expanded state) instead of stalling; pressing Down at the last line above a region behaves symmetrically; navigation past a region lands the caret in the correct adjacent plain-text line.

## Consumers

This directly extends the embedded-region behavior from task 002 inside the same RichTextBox-based prompt editor; no further downstream task depends on it.

completedWork: Verified Requirement 1 (Up at the first line below a region enters/passes it without stalling): PromptTextBox_KeyDown (MainWindow.xaml.cs:28054-28061) intercepts unmodified Up and calls RichTextBoxExtensions.TryFocusAdjacentEmbeddedCodeRegion(LogicalDirection.Backward), which locates the adjacent BlockUIContainer-hosted EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock via FindAdjacentEmbeddedCodeRegion (RichTextBoxExtensions.cs:431) and focuses its content.

Verified Requirement 2 (Down at the last line above a region behaves symmetrically): the same handler routes Down through LogicalDirection.Forward using block.ElementStart, with the smart-nav fallback TryNavigateIntoEmbeddedRegionWithDirection (RichTextBoxExtensions.cs:597) targeting the region's start/end position per direction.

Verified Requirement 3 (navigation past a region lands in the correct adjacent plain-text line): the dead-zone smart-nav path (MainWindow.xaml.cs:28066-28087) plus the pure, position-only EmbeddedCaretNavMath.Decide (EmbeddedCaretNavMath.cs:40, ExitForward/ExitBackward on first/last line) drive FocusHostOutsideRegion to the adjacent paragraph's ContentStart/ContentEnd.
Confirmed the key handler is actually wired via PreviewKeyDown="PromptTextBox_KeyDown" on PromptTextBox (MainWindow.xaml:3577), so the navigation logic is reachable at runtime.
Confirmed no manufactured edits: HEAD remains the task baseline a1452830 on the canonical branch with no pending source changes (only host-owned .squad/plans JSON is modified).

RichTextBoxExtensions.cs:399 TryFocusAdjacentEmbeddedCodeRegion and :431 FindAdjacentEmbeddedCodeRegion locate the BlockUIContainer-hosted EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock adjacent to the caret and call region.FocusContent().

claimFindings.claim: Req2 (Down above region, symmetric)
claimFindings.evidence: Same handler block at MainWindow.xaml.cs:28056 passes Forward for Key.Down. RichTextBoxExtensions.cs:544 FindRegionOnCaretParagraph and :597 TryNavigateIntoEmbeddedRegionWithDirection symmetrically detect the region on the destination paragraph and FocusContentAtPosition (0 for Down/Right, Content.Length for Up/Left).

claimFindings.claim: Req3 (lands in correct adjacent plain-text line)
claimFindings.evidence: EmbeddedCaretNavMath.Decide (EmbeddedCaretNavMath.cs:40,58-69) is a pure position-only decision returning ExitBackward on first line / ExitForward on last line. EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock.cs:409 FocusHostOutsideRegion and :444 FindHostCaretPointer move focus to the adjacent Paragraph's ContentStart (Forward) / ContentEnd (Backward), inserting a host paragraph via InsertHostParagraphWithoutUndo when none exists.

scrutinyHistory.testAssessment: Coverage genuinely exercises the boundary-navigation decision logic rather than passing trivially. EmbeddedCaretNavMathTests.cs directly asserts Decide() returns ExitBackward/ExitForward on first/last line and PassThrough for middle lines, selections, and non-boundary columns across empty, single-line, and multi-line text — the exact core of Req1/Req2/Req3. EmbeddedCodeRegionTests.cs adds integration coverage of FindAdjacentEmbeddedCodeRegion (adjacent true / non-adjacent null), FindRegionOnCaretParagraph (on-region vs off-region), and TryNavigateIntoEmbeddedRegionWithDirection_DownArrow_ReturnsTrue. The two MultilineRegion_*ShouldNotExit tests are weak (they assert content integrity, not the decision outcome), but the NavMath unit tests cover those non-exit middle-line cases properly, so the weakness is not a gap. Live WPF key routing cannot be fully proven headlessly, but per standard-level guidance the deterministic decision logic is covered and wired into the real PreviewKeyDown handlers, which is acceptable.
